questions.question:
Directions: Read the sentence to find out whether there is an error. The error, if any, will be in one part of the sentence. The number corresponding to that part will be your answer. If the given sentence is correct as it is, mark the answer as ‘No error’. Ignore any errors in punctuation, if any.

Neither of the (a)/ branch managers has (b)/ submitted their compliance report (c)/ to the headquarters.(d)/ No Error
questions.explanation:
• There is an error in part c of the given sentence.
  • With the use of ‘neither’ we need to use a singular pronoun in place of a plural one.
  • Hence, we need to replace ‘their’ with ‘his’.

Therefore, the correct answer is option C.

questions.question:
Directions: Read the sentence to find out whether there is an error. The error, if any, will be in one part of the sentence. The number corresponding to that part will be your answer. If the given sentence is correct as it is, mark the answer as ‘No error’. Ignore any errors in punctuation, if any.

I, you and Koushik (a) / must attend (b) / the digital meeting (c) / on career counseling. (d) / No Error
questions.explanation:
• There is an error in part ‘a’ of the sentence.
  • When three pronouns (different persons) are used in the same sentence and in the positive sense, they are arranged in order 2-3-1.
  • Thus, ‘You, Koushik and I’ should be used here.

Therefore, the correct answer is option C.

questions.question:
Directions: Study the following sentences and mark the erroneous part as your answer. In case there is no error, mark option (e), that is, ‘No Error’ as your answer.

It was 2010(a)/ that we (b)/first flew(c) /to Scotland.(d)/ No error
questions.explanation:
Let's break this down step by step:

  • (a) It was 2010: This part seems correct as it indicates the year.

  • (b) that we: This part also seems fine; it introduces the subordinate clause.

  • (c) first flew: This part indicates the action of flying for the first time, which seems correct.

  • (d) to Scotland: This part indicates the destination and seems correct as well.

Putting it all together, the sentence It was 2010 that we first flew to Scotland seems correct. Hence, there is no error.

The answer is: (e) No Error.

questions.question:
Directions: Study the following sentences and mark the erroneous part as your answer. In case there is no error, mark option (e), that is, ‘No Error’ as your answer.

Gayatri’s younger (a) / sister is (b)/ more intelligent (c)/ than her. (d) / No Error (e)
questions.explanation:
There is an error in part d of the sentence.

  • We need to replace 'her' with 'she'. We should note that in the case of pronouns coming after 'than', it must be in the same case as that coming before 'than'.
  • For instance, in the nominative case: You are better than I.
  • In the objective case: Shyamal respects you more than me.
  • The correct sentence should be: Gayatri’s younger sister is more intelligent than she.

Therefore, the correct answer is option C.

questions.question:
Direction: In the following question, one part of the sentence may have an error. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select ‘No Error’.

Employees should avail (A)/ of the opportunity to (B)/ buy cheap shares (C)/ in the company. (D)
questions.explanation:
Let's analyze the sentence step by step:

  • (A) Employees should avail: This part has an error. The correct usage is "avail themselves of" instead of just "avail."

  • (B) of the opportunity to: This part is correct.

  • (C) buy cheap shares: This part is correct.

  • (D) in the company: This part is correct.

The corrected sentence should be:

"Employees should avail themselves of the opportunity to buy cheap shares in the company."

The error is in part (A).

The answer is: (A).

questions.question:
Direction: In the following question, one part of the sentence may have an error. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select ‘No Error’.

If she'd protected their secret (A)/ from a thousand people, (B)/ she wasn't about to (C )/ reveal it to him. (D)
questions.explanation:
The sentence is free from error.

Explanation:

  • Part (A): "If she'd protected their secret" is grammatically correct. The contraction "she'd" stands for "she had," which is appropriate in this context.
  • Part (B): "from a thousand people" is correctly structured and aligns with the preceding clause.
  • Part (C): "she wasn't about to" is a valid expression indicating a firm intention not to do something.
  • Part (D): "reveal it to him" is properly formed and logically follows the sentence.

Correct Answer:

No Error

questions.question:

questions.explanation:

  • The pronoun 'him' is wrong here because the sentence talks about each and every sanitation worker, not just a particular worker.

Therefore, the correct answer is option b.

questions.question:
Directions: Study the following sentences and mark the erroneous part as your answer. In case there is no error, mark option (e), that is, ‘No Error’ as your answer.

Mrs Setupati availed (a)/of the opportunity (b)/that the company (c)/had provided to her.(d)/ No error
questions.explanation:
• There is an error in part ‘a’ of the given sentence.
  • We need to write ‘She availed herself of..’.
  • The pronoun ‘herself’ needs to be used here.
  • ‘Avail oneself of’ means ‘use or take advantage of an opportunity or available resource’.

Therefore, the correct answer is option C.

questions.question:
Directions: Study the following sentences and mark the erroneous part as your answer. In case there is no error, mark option (e), that is, ‘No Error’ as your answer.

The senior branch manager (a) / as well as the officers(b) / absented themselves (c) / the day before yesterday. (d) / No Error
questions.explanation:
• There is an error in part c of the given sentence.
  • We should note that we need to replace 'themselves' with 'himself'.
  • When two nouns are used with ‘as well as’, the pronoun must agree with the first subject.
  • In this case, the first subject is 'Senior Branch Manager', the correct pronoun to be used should be 'himself'.

The correct sentence should be: The Senior Branch manager as well as the officers absented himself the day before yesterday.

questions.question:
Directions: Study the following sentences and mark the erroneous part as your answer. In case there is no error, mark option (e), that is, ‘No Error’ as your answer.

Every officer(a) /and every clerk (b)/was ready with(c)/ their speech.(d)/No error
questions.explanation:
The error is in part (D) of the sentence.

Explanation:

  • The subject "Every officer and every clerk" is singular because "every" applies individually to each person. Therefore, the pronoun "their" in part (D) should be replaced with the singular pronoun "his or her" to maintain agreement.

Corrected Sentence:

  • Every officer and every clerk was ready with his or her speech.
  • The correct Answer is option (C).

questions.question:
Direction: In the following question, one part of the sentence may have an error. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select ‘No Error’.

He had access to his part much (A)/ earlier than me did, so (B)/ he was able to make some (C)/ investments that really paid off. (D)
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is option (B).

  • Subjective case comparison is always with a subjective case, and objective case comparison is always with an objective case.
  • Therefore, the error is in the comparison structure.
  • It should be "than I did" instead of "than me did."
  • When making a comparison, the pronoun "I" is used as the subject form, not "me."

questions.question:
Direction: In the following question, one part of the sentence may have an error. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select ‘No Error’.

There's still some (A)/ connection between (B)/ him and my mate, (C )/ isn't he? (D)
questions.explanation:
The error is in part (D) of the sentence.

Explanation:

In part (D), the question tag "isn't he" is incorrect because it does not match the subject of the main clause, which is "there". For the main clause "There's still some connection," the correct question tag should be "isn't there."

Corrected Sentence:

There's still some connection between him and my mate, isn't there?

Correct Answer:

(D)

questions.question:
Direction: Read the sentence to find out whether there is any error in it. The error, if any, will be in one part of the sentence. The number of that part is the answer. If there is no error, the answer is option E.

Corrected Sentence:

I will give you a novel tomorrow and it is written by one of the best selling authors.

Correct Answer:

Option (A)

questions.question:
Direction: Read the sentence to find out whether there is any error in it. The error, if any, will be in one part of the sentence. The number of that part is the answer. If there is no error, the answer is option E.

Arjun promised his father that he would never postpone things for him.

questions.question:
Direction: In the following question, one part of the sentence may have an error. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select ‘No Error’.

He was peppered with questions from the rescuers, (A)/ many of who he recognized, but he (B)/ held responses to a negative shake of his (C)/ head and Billy Langstrom's name. (D)
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is option (B).

  • Who and Whom are used for human beings, WHO is used for subjective cases, and WHOM is used for objective cases.
  • In this sentence, WHOM should be used instead of WHO to correctly indicate the object of the preposition "of."

questions.question:
Direction: In the following question, one part of the sentence may have an error. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select ‘No Error’.

I called he Black Beauty, as I had just read (A)/ the book, and he resembled his namesake (B)/ in every way, from his glossy black coat (C)/ to the white star on his forehead. (D)
questions.explanation:
Let's analyze the sentence step by step:

  • (A) I called he Black Beauty, as I had just read: This part contains an error. The correct pronoun should be "him" instead of "he." The correct form would be "I called him Black Beauty."

  • (B) the book, and he resembled his namesake: This part seems correct.

  • (C) in every way, from his glossy black coat: This part is correct.

  • (D) to the white star on his forehead: This part is correct.

"I called him Black Beauty, as I had just read the book, and he resembled his namesake in every way, from his glossy black coat to the white star on his forehead."

questions.question:
Direction: In the following question, one part of the sentence may have an error. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select ‘No Error’.

Once a nation shows their willingness to seize (A)/ foreign-owned property at will, foreign (B)/ investors are reluctant to (C)/ do business there again. (D)
questions.explanation:
The error is in part (A) of the sentence.

Explanation:

  • In part (A), the word "their" is incorrect because the subject "a nation" is singular and requires a singular pronoun. Instead of "their," it should be "its" to agree with the singular noun "nation."

Corrected Sentence:

  • Once a nation shows its willingness to seize foreign-owned property at will, foreign investors are reluctant to do business there again.

questions.question:
Directions: Study the following sentences and mark the erroneous part as your answer. In case there is no error, mark option (e), that is, ‘No Error’ as your answer.

questions.question:
Direction: In the following question, one part of the sentence may have an error. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select ‘No Error’.

Kings and queens which wear a suit but once, (A)/ though made by some tailor or dressmaker (B)/ to their majesties, cannot know (C)/ the comfort of wearing a suit that fits. (D)
questions.explanation:
The error is in part (A) of the sentence.

Explanation:

In part (A), the relative pronoun "which" is incorrect because it is used to refer to things, not people. Since the antecedent is "Kings and queens," the correct relative pronoun should be "who."

Corrected Sentence:

Kings and queens who wear a suit but once, though made by some tailor or dressmaker to their majesties, cannot know the comfort of wearing a suit that fits.

Correct Answer:

(A)

questions.question:
Direction: In the following question, one part of the sentence may have an error. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select ‘No Error’.

Betty-Boop or whatever your name is, if you tarry much (A)/ longer I may be forced to introduce, though (B)/ taking you, at least at this time, would cause a (C ) / mild alteration to my carefully formulated plans. (D)
questions.explanation:
The error is in part (B) of the sentence.

Explanation:

In part (B), the phrase "I may be forced to introduce, though" is incomplete and unclear. The verb "introduce" requires an object to indicate what is being introduced. The sentence seems to be missing clarity or a proper object after "introduce."

Corrected Sentence:

Betty-Boop or whatever your name is, if you tarry much longer, I may be forced to introduce myself, though taking you, at least at this time, would cause a mild alteration to my carefully formulated plans.

(B)

questions.question:
Direction: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Select option (E) if none of the option is correct. 

You, _______ and I are solving problems.
questions.explanation:
The given blank needs to be filled with a Pronoun.

  • Here, personal pronouns in the order of 2nd person, 3rd person, and 1st person will be used.
  • For good reason, the same order will be used.
  • For bad reasons or negative reasons, the order of 1st person, 2nd person, and 3rd person will be used.
    • See the example:
      • I, you, and she have committed this mistake.
  • Thus, the blank must be filled with ‘she’.

Hence, the correct sentence is: You, she, and I are solving problems.

questions.question:
Direction: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If there is no error select option (E) as your answer choice. 

The two friends were /quarrelling with one another /for distribution of money /in the market.
questions.explanation:
The given sentence is grammatically incorrect and the error lies in the option “quarrelling with one another”. The error is related to the “Pronoun”.

  • The subject of the given sentence is ‘The two friends’.
  • The Relative Pronoun ‘One another’ is used for more than two persons and things and ‘Each other’ is used to refer to ‘two persons and things’.
  • But in the given sentence, ‘one another’ is being used to refer to ‘two friends’ which is incorrect.
  • Therefore, we need to replace ‘one another’ with ‘each other’ to correct the sentence.
  • Example:
    • The two girls were talking to each other.
    • The countries are competing with one another to become the most powerful.

Hence, ‘one another’ should be replaced by ‘each other’ to make the sentence grammatically correct.

Correct sentence: The two friends were quarrelling with each other for distribution of money in the market.

questions.question:
Direction: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

I work mainly in the computer department, /who is / the smallest department / in  the University.
options: I work mainly in the computer department
questions.explanation:
The given sentence is grammatically incorrect and the error lies in the option “who is”. The error is related to the “Pronoun”.

  • In the given sentence the use of Pronoun "Who" is incorrect.
  • "Who" should be used to refer to the subject (persons) of a sentence.
  • For example:
    • The doctor appreciated the man who donated his heart.
  • Use "which" when referring to things, such as objects, animals, and places.
  • For example:
    • I wanted a good washing machine, which did all the basics, and the company recommended one that ticked all the boxes.
  • As per the need of the sentence we will use "which" to refer to the place i.e. university.
  • Hence, adjective "who" must be replaced by adjective "which" to make the sentence grammatically correct.

Correct sentence: I work mainly in the computer department, which is the smallest department in  the University.

questions.question:
Direction: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error from the given options.

If you play your cards right, the job could be your when she leaves.
questions.explanation:
The sentence is grammatically incorrect and the error lies in “the job could be your”. The error is related to the Pronoun.

"Your" is a possessive determiner that indicates ownership or possession of something and is used before a noun to show that the noun belongs to the person being addressed.

For example:

  • Your hat is on the table.
  • Can you please give me your phone number?
  • "Yours" is a possessive pronoun used to indicate possession of something and is used to replace a noun that has already been mentioned.
  • For example:
    • That red car is mine, and the blue one is yours.
  • Is this pen yours?
  • Hence, it should be replaced with ‘yours’ to form a correct answer.

Therefore, option A is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Direction: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error from the given options.

The essay is divided into five paragraphs and every of these has seven sentences.
questions.explanation:
The given statement is grammatically incorrect and the error lies in the option “and every of these”.

  • “Each” refers to an individual object or person, while the term “every” refers to a group of objects or people lumped together as one.
  • Here “every” is used incorrectly as the sentence refers to the individual paragraphs so it should be replaced with “each”.
  • Therefore, the error is in option D.

The correct statement: The essay is divided into five paragraphs and each of these has seven sentences.

questions.question:
Direction: In the following question, one part of the sentence may have an error. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select ‘No Error’.

The two boys across from her (A)/ had managed to make messes (B)/ of themself and the table in (C)/ what might have been a competition. (D)
questions.explanation:

  • (A) The two boys across from her: This part seems correct.

  • (B) had managed to make messes: This part also seems fine.

  • (C) of themself and the table in: This part contains an error. The correct reflexive pronoun for "the two boys" (plural) should be "themselves" instead of "themself."

  • (D) what might have been a competition: This part seems correct.

So, the error is in part (C). The corrected sentence should be:

"The two boys across from her had managed to make messes of themselves and the table in what might have been a competition."

questions.question:
Direction: In the following question, one part of the sentence may have an error. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select ‘No Error’.

The same instincts which warned her against (A)/ the last deal with him told her she'd (B)/ never win any bet with the devil I'll give (C)/ you the terms first this time. (D)
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is option (A).

  • The Same, the little, the few, none, etc., are definite clauses and always used with “THAT”.
  • Therefore, WHICH should be replaced with THAT.

Hence, the correct answer is A.

questions.question:
Direction: In the following question, one part of the sentence may have an error. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select ‘No Error’.

He soon changed his mind, (A)/ however, and, admitting them (B)/ to the circle of his intimates, (C)/ loaded them with your favours.(D)
questions.explanation:
Let's break down the sentence step by step:

  • (A) He soon changed his mind: This part seems correct.

  • (B) however, and, admitting them: This part also seems fine.

  • (C) to the circle of his intimates: This part is correct.

  • (D) loaded them with your favours: This part contains an error. The correct pronoun should be "his" instead of "your" because it should be consistent with "his intimates" in part C.

The corrected sentence should be:

"He soon changed his mind, however, and, admitting them to the circle of his intimates, loaded them with his favours."

The error is in part (D).

The answer is: (D).

questions.question:
Directions: In the following question, one part of the sentence may have an error. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select ‘No Error’.

She waited for him to leave (A)/ then checked her micro, (B)/ who was still working on (C)/ decrypting his encoded messages. (D)
questions.explanation:
Let's analyze the sentence step by step:

  • (A) She waited for him to leave: This part seems correct.

  • (B) then checked her micro: This part also seems correct.

  • (C) who was still working on: This part contains an error. The correct pronoun should be "which" instead of "who" because "micro" (most likely referring to a device) is not a person.

  • (D) decrypting his encoded messages: This part is correct.

The corrected sentence should be:

"She waited for him to leave, then checked her micro, which was still working on decrypting his encoded messages."

questions.question:
Directions: In the following question, one part of the sentence may have an error. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select ‘No Error’.

I spent forty minutes alone with (A)/ the director and related all (B)/ the situations where yours (C)/ uncanny tips were involved. (D)
questions.explanation:
The error lies in part C of the sentence.

  • In this context, "your"  should be used as a possessive adjective modifying the noun "uncanny tips."
  • The possessive form "your" is used before a noun to indicate ownership or association.
  • The correct possessive form in this case is "your," and "yours" (as a pronoun) is not necessary because "uncanny tips" is the noun in question.

Hence, option C is the correct choice.

questions.question:
Directions: Study the following sentences and mark the erroneous part as your answer. In case there is no error, mark option (e), that is, ‘No Error’ as your answer.

Mr Puneet ordered the (a) / security guard to (b) / let the men (c) / and I go into the room. (d) / No Error.
questions.explanation:
• There is an error in part d of the sentence.
  • We should replace 'I' with 'me'. After the word 'let', pronouns are always used in the objective case.
  • Similarly, after prepositions like between, except, etc, pronouns are always used in the objective case.

The grammatically correct sentence should be: Mr Puneet ordered the security guard to let the men and me go into the room.

Therefore, the correct answer is option C.

questions.question:
Direction: In the following question, one part of the sentence may have an error. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select ‘No Error’.

Here, then, I made my home; (A)/ and although it is a lonely place I (B)/ amuse making rustles and flutters, (C)/ and so get along very nicely. (D)
questions.explanation:
The error is in part (C) of the sentence.

Explanation:

In part (C), the phrase "amuse making rustles and flutters" is incorrect. The verb "amuse" should be followed by a reflexive pronoun (e.g., "myself") to indicate that the subject is entertaining themselves. The corrected phrase should be "amuse myself by making rustles and flutters."

Corrected Sentence:

Here, then, I made my home; and although it is a lonely place, I amuse myself by making rustles and flutters, and so get along very nicely.

questions.question:
Direction: In the following question, one part of the sentence may have an error. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select ‘No Error’.

questions.explanation:
The error is in part (D) of the sentence.

Explanation:

  • In part (D), the word "whom" is incorrect because it is used as the object of a verb or preposition, but in this case, the relative pronoun refers to the subject of the verb "had emerged." The correct word should be "who."

Corrected Sentence:

  • These were very numerous, for the place was thickly inhabited, and a large group of the queer people clustered near, gazing sharply upon the strangers who had emerged from the long spiral stairway.

  • How differences between men and women might be used for our mutual benefit in everything from our relations with each other to a better understanding of how our brains work.

questions.question:

Martha and Quinn were readying (A)/ for our restaurant dinner in its (B)/ room and Betsy was upstairs (C)/ usurping the single bathroom. (D)
questions.explanation:

Corrected Sentence:

Martha and Quinn were readying for our restaurant dinner in their room, and Betsy was upstairs usurping the single bathroom.

Correct Answer:

(B)

questions.question:
Direction: In the following question, one part of the sentence may have an error. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select ‘No Error’.

Well, say your father has a German valet, (A)/ and he is a splendid valet and satisfies your father's (B)/ requirements better than you could, (C) / then it's all right to let he serve.(D)
questions.explanation:

Directions: In the following question, a sentence has been divided into four parts, one of which may contain an error. Identify the part that contains the error and mark it as your answer. If the sentence is correct as it is, choose 'No Error' as your answer. Ignore errors in punctuation, if any. 

The Wizard opened his satchel and (A)/ got out some sticking-plaster with (B)/ whom he mended the cuts Jim had (C)/ received from the claws of the bears. (D)
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Option C.

Part C is erroneous due to the incorrect usage of "whom," which should be replaced with "which."

"Whom" is a relative pronoun used exclusively for people. "Sticking-plaster" is a non-living thing — an object — and objects are always referred to using "which" not "whom." Using "whom" for a non-living object is a fundamental pronoun error.

Parts A, B and D are all grammatically and contextually correct and need no change.

The correct sentence would be — The Wizard opened his satchel and got out some sticking-plaster with which he mended the cuts Jim had received from the claws of the bears.

Additional Information

Who/Whom vs Which: "who" and "whom" are used only for people while "which" is used for non-living things and animals. Mixing them up is one of the most commonly tested errors in banking exams 

  • For Example — She is the person who helped me. / This is the tool with which I fixed the machine.

With which: a fixed phrase used to describe an instrument or object used to perform an action

  • For Example — He handed me the pen with which I had to sign the documen
